newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF HEARTS PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF HEARTS PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the players most likely to play for Heart of Midlothian against Glasgow Rangers in a Scottish premier division match on Saturday.

Gilles Rousset (goalkeeper, age 33). Former Sochaux, Lyon and Marseilles goalkeeper who has played twice for France. Joined Hearts in October 1995 and has established himself as a firm favourite with fans at Tynecastle. Let a harmless cross from Brian Laudrup dribble through his legs and into the goal when Hearts met Rangers in the Scottish Cup final in May. Think twice before reminding Rousset of that though -- at six-foot-five (196 cm) he is an imposing figure.

Stephen Frail (defender, 27). Attack-minded defender who spent eight years at Dundee before joining Hearts in 1994. Missed a large chunk of last season with a ligament injury but is now back to full fitness and challenging for a place in the side.

David Weir (defender, 26). Highly-rated centre-back who followed Hearts manager Jim Jeffries to Tynecastle from Falkirk. An outside tip for international honours after a number of rock-solid performances for his new club. Can play in midfield as well as defence.

Pasquale Bruno (defender, 34). Stylish defender now in the twilight of his career. Chalked up over 300 serie A appearances with Fiorentina, Juventus and Torino before moving to Hearts where he settled immediately. One of the "group of four" Hearts players sent off in a heated match against Rangers in September.

Dave McPherson (defender, 32). One match for whom this fixture means an awful lot. Signed for Hearts from Rangers in 1988, moved back to Ibrox in 1992 only to rejoin Hearts two years later. Has played 27 times for Scotland, including all three matches in the World Cup in Italy in 1990. Has over 300 appearances for Hearts to his name.

Neil Pointon (midfielder, 32). Powerful Englishman who started his career with Manchester City before moving to Howard Kendall's successful Everton side of the mid-1980s. Won an English league championship medal with the Merseysiders in 1987. Moved on to Oldham before crossing the border to join Hearts in October 1995.

Jeremy Goss (midfielder, 31). Welsh international who spent 14 years at English side Norwich before moving north of the border to round off his career. Has struggled with injury since arriving in Edinburgh.

Steve Fulton (midfielder, 26. Cultured midfielder who started his career at Glasgow Celtic before moving to English side Bolton. Jeffries brought him back to Scotland last season in a swap deal with David Hagen. Has missed games through injury this season but is now back on form.
Colin Cameron (midfielder, 23). Scotland B international who signed from Raith Rovers in March 1996. Has scored a number of vital goals in recent matches.
Alan McManus (midfielder, 22). Product of the Hearts youth team policy who broke into the first team in December 1995.

Darren Beckford (forward, 28). Powerful striker who, like Pointon, started at Manchester City and moved to Oldham before signing for Hearts in August 1996. Also enjoyed spells south of the border with Port Vale and Norwich. Endeared himself to Tynecastle fans immediately by scoring a vital penalty on his debut.

Neil McCann (forward, 21). Highly-rated and exciting Scotland under-21 international who signed from Dundee in a suprise move just before the start of the current season. Has laboured under a thigh injury recently but is recovering fast.

John Colquhoun (forward, 33). Charismatic forward who has ambitions to move into politics after hanging up his boots. A former chairman of the Scottish Players' Association, he is a regular columnist with the Scotland on Sunday newspaper. Enjoying his second spell at Hearts after a career that has taken him to Stirling and Celtic as well as English clubs Sunderland and Millwall.

John Robertson (forward, 32). Has been at Tynecastle since leaving school apart from a short-lived spell south of the border at Newcastle in 1988. The club's top scorer in every season he has played, Robertson is closing in on the club's record goal tally of 206, set by Jimmy Wardhaugh between 1946-59. Has won 16 caps for Scotland.
